newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Call options bought in BT.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Call options bought in BT.

text.p: Options traders took advantage of the weakness in British Telecommunications shares on Monday in order to buy call options, in the belief the underlying stock will rally in the weeks ahead, dealers said.

BT's proposed $20 billion merger with America's MCI Communications -- to create a single company called Concert plc -- has left BT's share price lagging slightly as investors have arbitraged between the two company's by buying MCI shares and selling BT.
But some traders believe the situation may change and that BT's share price is ready to step up a gear.
One deal in BT options was to was to buy 1,000 May 460 calls at 8p. Another was to buy 500 May 420 calls at about 28p.

The terms of the proposed merger are that for each MCI shares held, 0.54 new Concert American Depositary Shares (ADS) -- the same as 0.54 BT ADS's representing 10 BT shares -- plus a cash payment of $6.0 would be made. ($=0.617 British pounds).
By 1355 GMT, BT shares were down 4-1/2p to 437p.

In retailer Marks & Spencer, the main options deal was from a seller of 700 June 500 calls at 11p to protect against losses from a shareholding in M&S if the share price slips. M&S shares were down 2-1/2p to 492p.
Over in shipping and transportation group P&O, there was a buyer of 500 May 600 calls at 21p, hoping the underlying shares will bounce. P&O shares added 5p to 607-1/2p.

And in conglomerate Lonrho, the main deal was the sale of 400 December 140 puts at 5p indicating a willingness to buy the shares at 140p -- owing to being assigned the puts -- if the stock price is below the strike price, which it now is.
